name: IB vs RAW Institutional Friction (India)
alternate_names: Intelligence Bureau vs Research and Analysis Wing
description: Persistent bureaucratic and operational rivalry between India's two primary intelligence agencies: Intelligence Bureau (IB, domestic focus, under Home Ministry) and Research and Analysis Wing (RAW, external focus, under Cabinet Secretariat). This friction creates intelligence gaps, operational inefficiencies, and security vulnerabilities — particularly in transnational threats where domestic-external boundaries blur.

intelligence_bureau.legal_basis: Indian Police Service cadre, no statutory charter
intelligence_bureau.primary_mandate: Domestic intelligence, counter-intelligence, counter-terrorism within India
intelligence_bureau.director_appointment: Senior IPS officer, typically with state/territorial policing background

raw.primary_mandate: Foreign intelligence, external security, counter-terrorism outside India
raw.director_appointment: Senior IPS or specialized intelligence cadre; historically includes military intelligence

sources_of_friction.jurisdictional_overlap: Transnational terror (Pakistan-based groups attacking India) falls into gap; IB claims domestic aftermath, RAW claims foreign origin
sources_of_friction.resource_competition: Budget allocations, technical assets, human sources
sources_of_friction.cadre_differences: IB traditional police intelligence culture vs RAW 'operational' culture; mutual professional disdain
sources_of_friction.information_hoarding: Both agencies classify intelligence to protect sources/methods, creating national-level blind spots
sources_of_friction.bureaucratic_incentives: Credit for success, blame avoidance for failure — inter-agency coordination risks both

historical_manifestations.consequence: Khalistani groups exploited intelligence gaps between state police, IB, and RAW border operations
RAW criticized for not detecting Pakistani infiltration; IB role in domestic early warning unclear
JeM external planning (RAW jurisdiction) converged with Delhi domestic cell (IB) — coordination gaps documented
External planning in Pakistan (RAW) and maritime insertion (coastal IB/Coast Guard coordination failure)
NSA coordinates both agencies; institutional friction persists but operational coordination reportedly improved

ajit_doval.significance: First IB officer to become NSA; theoretically bridges IB-RAW gap; represents IB institutional interests at highest level

as_dulat.significance: Advocate of 'strategic patience' and negotiation (Kashmir); represents RAW's intelligence-first vs action-first divide

ks_bhullar_character.real_anchor: A.S. Dulat — institutional friction with IB Director Sanyal (Doval parallel) in Film 1

ajay_sanyal_character.real_anchor: Ajit Doval as IB Director — operational vs strategic intelligence tension with Bhullar

film_relevance.dhurandhar_1_tension: KS Bhullar (RAW) vs Ajay Sanyal (IB) — institutional friction subplot. Bhullar 'strategic patience' vs Sanyal 'operational action'.
film_relevance.dhurandhar_2_resolution: Naya Bharat mandate expansion — Sanyal elevated, coordination mechanism imposed
film_relevance.operational_consequence: Hamza's infiltration faces dual oversight friction; intelligence may not flow optimally between IB domestic sources and RAW operational support
film_relevance.narrative_function: Realistic institutional constraint on protagonist; explains why Indian response isn't perfectly coordinated

oracle_implications.for_hamza: Dual reporting creates cover-integrity risk; inconsistent handler instructions possible
oracle_implications.for_rizwan: Sanyal's elevation in Film 2 may provide clearer chain of command; opportunity for more decisive action
oracle_implications.optimization_insight: Pipeline should recommend single-point command structure to reduce agency friction
